$doc: The codes the renderer's WebGPU calls and the host that makes them agree on
(gpu/api.rs, apps/web/src/platform/web/webgpu.ts). Usage flags are WebGPU's own
bits, spelled out where they are used, and are not here.
A texture's format: the texture pack, skins and the badge sheet; depth; the
canvas's own; then the screen-space occlusion's — a half-resolution depth and
normal in four floats, the full-resolution occlusion in one byte, and the blue
noise it dithers with, four bytes read as they are; then the atmosphere's
tables, radiance and transmittance in four half floats, filterable and
renderable on every WebGPU device.
A sampler's comparison: none for a filtering sampler, less-equal for the shadow map's.
What a bind group entry binds.
What a canvas the shell hands over shows (gpu/surface.rs): the world, or one thing in a case.
An attachment's start: cleared, loaded, or a depth read and not written.
The one place the renderer's calls cross (gpu/api.rs): a stream
(xpute-guest ipc/stream.rs) in a range of the kernel's memory, which the
kernel writes its calls into during a turn and the host runs once the turn
has returned. A record carries everything it names, bytes included, so
nothing a record reads lies outside it.
Its head is HEAD words: the stream's END, then from GPU_MS, the host's side,
each timed span's GPU time in milliseconds as a double, then the frame's
whole, as the host last read them.
The range's size: what one turn may send the device. A product number, said
rather than derived; a chunk's mesh is under a tenth of a megabyte and a
frame's own records tens of kilobytes, so a turn's uploads wait only when
a burst of them comes at once.
What an upload leaves of the range. The records a turn cannot put off — a
frame's passes and draws, the shaders the first frame makes — are never
refused, so an upload, which can wait a turn, is taken only while this much
is left after it.
A pass's timestamp write index (api.rs Stamp): NONE where the pass writes none.
A record's operation, then its arguments. Bytes go as their count, then the bytes padded to a word.

encoder, id, offset, length, address, word, ticket: the buffer's bytes from offset, once the GPU has them, copied into the module's memory at address, and the word at `word` marked `read.DONE` over the ticket; only while that word still holds the ticket, so a range asked of again since takes the later answer alone
What READ_BUFFER leaves in its word: the ticket asked, with DONE set once the bytes are in. A ticket leaves DONE clear.
A pipeline record's codes (shader.rs), and HEAD, the words it opens with
before its vertex buffers — the one number three parsers of a record would
otherwise each hold their own copy of. Then: the topology, the cull mode, the
depth compare under reversed Z (LESS is the shadow map's plain depth; NO_DEPTH, no
depth attachment), the blend, which vertex entry point of
its shader the pipeline enters, a vertex step and format, a
binding's stages, and a binding's kind — TEXTURE_UNFILTERED a texture in a
format no sampler
filters (RGBA32F), read by textureLoad alone.
